descriptionChirho: An enclitic coordinating particle that connects clauses, phrases, or words, typically appearing postpositively. In its primary use (211 of 215 occurrences) it functions as a simple connective 'and' or correlative 'both...and' (τε...καί, τε...τε). Occasional contextual renderings as 'also' (3x) or 'even' (1x) reflect translation choices rather than distinct lexical senses. Spanish renders it as connective markers 'y/también'; Hindi 'और/भी' both serve as coordinating connectives; Arabic 'وَ' is the standard conjunction throughout; Korean '그리고' (and) is consistent; Swahili 'na/pia/hata' range from 'and' to 'also' to 'even' but all express the same additive conjunction. The three clusters represent no semantic distinction — all are the same enclitic particle τε functioning as a lightweight connective, with minor translational variation driven by context rather than meaning.
